To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) BIGRUs with attention and label embeddings outperformed other state of the art classifiers, (2) domain specific embeddings further improved the performance of BIGRU, (3) BERT can be used to classify legal texts, but its maximum text length limit needs to be bypassed, and (4) the best results in few shot learning were obtained with BERT, while in zero shot learning BIGRU performed best.

(i) BIGRU with label-wise attention performs better than current state of the arts in LMTC; (ii) domain specific word2vec and elmo embeddings further improve performance; (iii) fine tuned BERT with only a subset of the document text achieves better performance; (iv) zero shot learning performance is poor.
BIGRUs, with label wise attention, and domain specific embeddings, perform best in the LMTC task.
